In 1993, Chile adopted an Indigenous Law that enabled land restitution; by 2023...
articles.description: Since 1993, over 510,000 acres have been returned to Mapuche communities in Chile under the Indigenous Law. A study revealed minimal changes in forest cover on the restituted lands. It observed a decline in commercial plantations and a slight rise in agricultural pastures, emphasizing the importance of traditional economic practices alongside conservation. This situation illustrates the need for distinct strategies in managing land rights and environmental restoration efforts.

articles.title: In 1988, an English farmer stopped cultivating his entire 377-acre wheat farm
articles.description: An abandoned wheat farm in England has been transformed into a thriving nature reserve after decades of neglect. Following a dedicated public campaign, £1.5 million was raised to acquire the land, ensuring its protection for future generations. This 377-acre area now boasts a rich variety of wildlife, including numerous endangered bird species, and will be overseen by the Wildlife Trust as a cherished habitat.

articles.title: From writing code to growing mushrooms: How this BTech graduate left IT after 14 years to build a farming business earning over Rs 10 lakh a month
articles.description: After 14 years in the IT industry, BTech graduate Vikramdev Mohapatra left his corporate career to return to Nabarangpur, Odisha, and build a commercial mushroom farming business. His venture, Ganga Bhumi Mushrooms, produces 500–600 kg of mushrooms daily and supplies markets in Brahmapur and Bhubaneswar. With monthly revenue reportedly reaching Rs 16–19 lakh, the enterprise earns over Rs 10 lakh after expenses and employs 24 people, including 18 women, showcasing rural entrepreneurship and job creation.

articles.title: The history student who changed physics forever: The PhD thesis Albert Einstein said had ‘lifted a corner of the great veil’
articles.description: Louis de Broglie began as a history student before turning toward mathematics and physics, ultimately reshaping modern science. In his 1924 PhD thesis, he proposed that particles such as electrons possess wave-like properties, challenging established ideas about matter. Experiments later confirmed his hypothesis, helping establish a foundation for quantum mechanics. De Broglie received the 1929 Nobel Prize in Physics, and his work influenced Schrödinger’s wave mechanics and technologies such as electron microscopes.
